from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows", [
            "Vectors are directed segments in 2D space.",
            "Moving: v = [2, 1] means right 2, up 1.",
            "Scaling and adding vectors build everything."
        ])

        # Define coordinate axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create vectors
        v_coords = [2, 1]
        w_coords = [-1, 2]
        
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(*v_coords), color="#FF5733", buff=0)
        w = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(*w_coords), color="#33FF57", buff=0)
        
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#FF5733").next_to(v.get_end(), RIGHT)
        w_label = MathTex(r"\vec{w}", color="#33FF57").next_to(w.get_end(), LEFT)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(FadeIn(v), Write(v_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.play(FadeIn(w), Write(w_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        
        # Parallelogram Rule
        v_to_w = Arrow(start=v.get_end(), end=axes.c2p(*(np.array(v_coords)+np.array(w_coords))), color="#33FF57", buff=0, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        w_to_v = Arrow(start=w.get_end(), end=axes.c2p(*(np.array(v_coords)+np.array(w_coords))), color="#FF5733", buff=0, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        sum_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(*(np.array(v_coords)+np.array(w_coords))), color="#3357FF", buff=0)
        
        self.play(Create(v_to_w), Create(w_to_v), GrowArrow(sum_vec))
        self.play(v.animate.set_color(WHITE), w.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3357FF")

        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Basis", [
            "Basis is the minimal spanning set.",
            "Linearly independent vectors efficiently define space.",
            "Basis is the most efficient coordinate system."
        ])

        j_hat = Vector(UP, color="#33FF57")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        # Define target point (3, 2)
        target = 3 * i_hat.get_vector() + 2 * j_hat.get_vector()
        
        self.play(
            i_hat.animate.scale(3, about_point=ORIGIN),
            j_hat.animate.scale(2, about_point=ORIGIN),
            run_time=2
        )
        # Shift j_hat to (3,0)
        self.play(j_hat.animate.shift(3 * RIGHT))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors build combinations.", "Combinations create a span.", "Redundancy removal reveals the basis."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define table elements
        span_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        span_text = Text("Span", font_size=24)
        span_group = VGroup(span_rect, span_text)
        
        dep_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=RED).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.3)
        dep_text = Text("Dependence", font_size=24)
        dep_group = VGroup(dep_rect, dep_text)
        
        basis_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        basis_text = Text("Basis", font_size=24)
        basis_group = VGroup(basis_rect, basis_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(span_group, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(span_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(dep_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(dep_group))
        line1 = Line(span_group.get_right(), dep_group.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_group, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(basis_group))
        line2 = Line(dep_group.get_bottom(), basis_group.get_top(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line2))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(span_group, dep_group, basis_group, line1, line2, self.lecture))
        self.title.move_to(ORIGIN)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed segments in 2D space. Visualize them as movements: v = [2, 1] is 'go right 2, up 1'. Establish that scaling (c*v) and addition (v+w) form the building blocks of all operations.
sections.example: A delivery drone moving along vector A (North) and vector B (East).

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define a linear combination as 'c1v1 + c2v2'. Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible reach points. Use a grid animation: show the drone moving in varying steps of A and B, gradually filling the entire 2D plane.
sections.example: Two vectors A=[1,0] and B=[0,1] act as building blocks; by combining them, the drone can reach any point (x, y) on the map.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
sections.content: Explain linear dependence visually: if vector C lies on the same line as A and B, it adds no 'new' dimensions. It is redundant. Use an animation showing a third vector being 'squashed' into the existing line.
sections.example: Three robots walking: Robot C follows the exact path of Robot A. If Robot A is already there, Robot C provides no new navigation capability.

sections.title: The Concept of Basis
sections.content: Define a Basis as the 'minimal set' of vectors that span the space without redundancy (linearly independent). Emphasize that a basis is the most efficient 'coordinate system' for a space.
sections.example: To describe a room, you need exactly 3 dimensions (Length, Width, Height). If you add a 4th measurement that is just a sum of the others, it's not a basis—it's redundant information.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Wrap up by linking the concepts: Vectors build Combinations -> Combinations create a Span -> Removing redundant vectors leaves us with a Basis. Connect back to the drone navigation example.
sections.example: A GPS system uses a basis of 3 satellites to pinpoint any position in 3D space. Adding a 4th satellite makes the system more robust but technically redundant for the base span.
